from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Towers of Hanoi Puzzle", [
            "Move disks from start to end peg.",
            "Never place larger disks on smaller ones.",
            "Move one disk at a time only."
        ])

        # Setup pegs and disks
        peg_a = Line(DOWN, UP).shift(self.grid["D2"])
        peg_b = Line(DOWN, UP).shift(self.grid["D4"])
        peg_c = Line(DOWN, UP).shift(self.grid["D6"])
        
        pegs = VGroup(peg_a, peg_b, peg_c)
        
        disk_sizes = [1.2, 0.9, 0.6]
        disks = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=size, height=0.2, color=BLUE).next_to(peg_a, DOWN, buff=0) for size in disk_sizes])
        
        # Stacking logic
        for i, disk in enumerate(disks):
            if i > 0:
                disk.next_to(disks[i-1], DOWN, buff=0)
        
        full_setup = VGroup(pegs, disks)
        self.place_in_area(full_setup, "B2", "E6", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.add(full_setup)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(RED))
        
        # Highlight smallest disk
        smallest_disk = disks[2]
        self.play(smallest_disk.animate.set_color("#FF4500"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        
        # Move smallest disk from Peg A to Peg C
        target_pos = peg_c.get_bottom() + np.array([0, 0.1, 0])
        self.play(smallest_disk.animate.move_to(target_pos))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mapping Moves to Binary", [
            "- Hanoi moves match the binary sequence.",
            "- Three disks require seven total moves.",
            "- Binary count zero-zero-one is move one.",
            "- Binary count one-one-one is move seven.",
            "- The sequence maps binary to disk movement."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        move_label = Text("Move:", font_size=32)
        binary_display = Text("000", font_size=64, color="#00CED1")
        self.place_at_grid(move_label, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(binary_display, 'B4')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00CED1"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00CED1"))
        new_val = Text("001", font_size=64, color="#00CED1")
        self.place_at_grid(new_val, 'B4')
        self.play(Transform(binary_display, new_val))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF4500"))

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Small disks move every other turn.",
            "Middle disks move every four turns.",
            "Large disks move every eight turns.",
            "Smallest disk moves at every odd step.",
            "Movement follows a perfect recursive pattern."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Algorithmic Logic", lecture_lines)

        # Formula Mobjects
        formula = MathTex("T(n) = 2T(n-1) + 1", font_size=48)
        formula.set_color_by_tex("2", "#32CD32")
        formula.set_color_by_tex("1", "#32CD32")
        
        # Branching tree visualization
        tree = VGroup(
            Circle(radius=0.3, color=BLUE).move_to(ORIGIN),
            Line(ORIGIN, UP*1 + LEFT*1.5),
            Line(ORIGIN, UP*1 + RIGHT*1.5),
            Circle(radius=0.2, color=BLUE).move_to(UP*1 + LEFT*1.5),
            Circle(radius=0.2, color=BLUE).move_to(UP*1 + RIGHT*1.5)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'B2', 'B5', scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(FadeIn(tree))
        self.place_in_area(tree, 'D2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(tree.animate.shift(DOWN*0.5).scale(1.2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(FadeOut(formula), FadeOut(tree))

outline.topic: Binary Counting and the Towers of Hanoi: The Mathematical Secret

sections.title: The Binary Language (Prerequisite)
sections.content: Introduce binary (base-2) as a system using only 0 and 1. Explain that each digit position represents a power of 2 (1, 2, 4, 8...). Visualize this using 'Light Switches': ON=1, OFF=0.
sections.example: A 3-bit system: 001 (1), 010 (2), 011 (3), 100 (4). Animation: 3 switches toggling like a dance.

sections.title: The Towers of Hanoi Puzzle
sections.content: Define the goal: Move a stack of N disks from Peg A to Peg C, moving only one at a time and never placing a larger disk on a smaller one.
sections.example: A monkey trying to move a 3-disk 'banana pyramid' from one tree to another following the strict rules.

sections.title: Mapping Moves to Binary
sections.content: Explain the surprising link: The sequence of disk moves corresponds exactly to the binary counting sequence. The number of moves required for N disks is 2^N - 1.
sections.example: For 3 disks: 2^3 - 1 = 7 moves. Animation showing the move number (1-7) appearing as binary numbers (001 to 111) alongside the disk movement.

sections.title: The Algorithmic Logic
sections.content: Explain that the n-th disk moves exactly once, at step 2^(n-1). This explains why the rhythm of the puzzle is patterned—the smallest disk moves every other turn.
sections.example: A visual 'Clock' where the small hand (disk 1) moves every tick, the middle hand (disk 2) every 2 ticks, and the large hand (disk 3) every 4 ticks.

sections.title: Summary and Real-world Application
sections.content: Conclude by connecting the puzzle to computer science algorithms (recursion) and data storage. Remind students that binary isn't just counting—it's the 'DNA' of logical movement.
sections.example: Showing a computer chip or a server rack processing data packets as if they were disks in a Hanoi tower.
